prefixVerifier.scope: All initial encoded files and manifests authenticated; changed old-prefix BlockRecords decoded and byte-compared at one captured revision. bytes_hashed counts explicit digest passes, not total I/O.

oldLayoutSnapshotProbe.scope: ordinary core execute_query plus JSON serialization; no HTTP or source-readiness override; warm caches

startup.comparability: One observation per process. CPU ceilings and concurrent work differ; caches were not cleared. Neither admission nor refresh is presented as a paired speedup or guaranteed cold startup.

limitations: The original HTTP reader remains deployed and was not restarted; its schema3/ZREF1 compatibility was checked before catalog publication.
Source epochs also invalidate physical-layout cursors. HTTP409duringlayoutchanges andcapacity429responses remain in samples; canonicality/read gates were not bypassed.
Follow publishes before one bounded consolidation; source observations after layout changes come from real RPC and canonical-head checks.
Retired segments and all79initialunreferenced directories remain. Disk growth is bounded by configured budgets; garbage collection requires separate reader quiescence.
The earlier recovery acceptance precedes the completed observation and final soft-threshold acceptance; every point remains timestamped.
The first prefix proof captured epoch90; the final independent proof captured epoch178 after soft-threshold headroom was restored. Future appends remain outside those captured snapshots.
Core query samples are sequential warm-cache reads; HTTP samples include actual queue/refresh/serialization effects and are separately scoped.
The later steady-state acceptance restores count/byte soft-threshold headroom; its second full-prefix proof and final query cohort are separate from the earlier recovery snapshots.

postMaintenanceQueries.scope: Separate post-soft-threshold loopback observation, not pooled with the recovery phases or a controlled speedup comparison. Final prefix verifier active concurrently.
